# Technique — RESPx re-strobing: eight copies a scanline, not three

**Goal:** put more shaped slots on one scanline than NUSIZ alone gives. Two players with three
copies each is six; re-strobing takes one player to eight, and two players to sixteen. That is the
floor under any dense-text kernel (`text12.md`, `text24.md`, `bitmap48.md`).

**Status:** ✅ measured and CI-locked. Fixture `roms/litmus/litmus_restrobe.asm` (generated by
`scripts/gen_litmus_restrobe.py`); grading `internal/emu/restrobe_test.go`.
**Source:** `reference/atariage/180632-32-character-text-display` records solidcorp's 2011
32-character display and files this mechanism as **candidate ⑨, unverified** — "re-strobe
RESP0/RESP1 several times a line with NUSIZ at three copies close and the copy sequence restarts".
Measured here 2026-08-25, from private `roms/` work that had concluded six shaped slots was a
hardware ceiling and went looking for why.

**Cycle convention is this catalogue's:** `c` is the **write cycle** — the last of the three cycles
of `sta RESPx` — and a normal-width player lands at **`x = 3c − 60`** (`sprite-placement.md` rule 1).

## The ladder

`litmus_restrobe` parks P0 at x=3 with NUSIZ=3 (three copies, sixteen apart) while the screen is
still blank, then band k re-strobes RESP0 k times on ONE picture line, eight cycles apart:

| re-strobes | write cycles | copies drawn on that one scanline | count |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | — | 3, 19, 35 | 3 |
| 1 | 29 | 3, 19, 43, 59 | 4 |
| 2 | 29, 37 | 3, 19, 43, 67, 83 | 5 |
| 3 | 29, 37, 45 | 3, 19, 43, 67, 91, 107 | 6 |
| 4 | 29, 37, 45, 53 | 3, 19, 43, 67, 91, 115, 131 | 7 |
| 5 | 29, 37, 45, 53, 61 | 3, 19, 43, 67, 91, 115, 139, 155 | 8 |

**3 + k.** The strobe does not move the copies already drawn; it starts another run of them.

## Why a strobe is worth exactly one more copy

This is `sprite-placement.md` **rule 8** — "a strobe cancels the pending draw of the FIRST copy
only" — seen from the other side, and the ladder is what rule 8 is worth when you use it on purpose.

Take band 1. The player is parked at 3, so its copies are 3, 19, 35. The strobe's write cycle is 29,
which puts the beam at `3·29 − 68 = 19` and the new base at `3·29 − 60 = 27`. What is drawn is
**3, 19, 43, 59**:

- **3 and 19 survive** — already drawn when the strobe ran, so nothing can reach back for them.
- **35 is lost.** It had not been drawn yet, and the strobe restarts the copy counter.
- **27 is lost** — the new base, cancelled by rule 8.
- **43 and 59 draw** — the +16 and +32 the new base makes.

One lost, two gained. **Net +1, and it stays +1 for every further strobe**, which is what the ladder
measures. The eight-cycle spacing in the fixture is not special; any spacing at or above three
cycles works, and three cycles is the floor because that is one `sta`.

Two consequences bind every kernel built on this, and the test grades both:

- **An added copy is never at `x ≡ 0 (mod 3)`.** A base is `3c − 60`, always a multiple of three, so
  the copies that survive — base+16 and base+32 — land at ≡ 1 and ≡ 2. A row of letters at a uniform
  pitch needs every residue; the ones at ≡ 0 can only come from an object's **parked** base, one per
  object, or from shifting the glyph inside its byte, which a w-pixel letter can do by up to 8 − w.
- **The leading two copies are fixed** at the parked base and base+16. Only what comes after the
  first strobe is yours to place.

## What it costs

`203487_36char.bin` (attached to that thread; disassembled here with `cmd/beamtrace`) spends one
scanline like this:

```
cycle  0   RESP0            the line opens with one
      14   GRP0 = $55
      20   GRP1 = $75
      26   GRP0 = $44
      32   GRP0 = $21
      42   GRP1 = $55
      48   GRP1 = $55
      51   RESP0            mid-line
      54   GRP0 = $A4
      57   RESP0            and again
      61   GRP0 = $A8
      67   GRP0 = $AA
      73   HMP1 = $80
```

Nine GRP writes, three strobes, ending at cycle 73 of 76 — **the budget is spent, not merely used.**
The writes sit six cycles apart, which is `lda zp` (3) plus `sta GRPx` (3); the 3–3–3 burst in the
middle is stores from registers already loaded. Every byte is a pair of nibbles (`$77` = 7,7;
`$E4` = E,4), so a slot is two characters at 4 px.

**Count the slots on the screen rather than the writes in the listing.** Decomposing two adjacent
scanlines of that ROM (65 and 66, `emu.DecomposeRow`):

```
line 65 slots:    28   44   60   76   92  100  116  132
line 66 slots: 20   36   52   68   84       108  124  140
union        : 20 28 36 44 52 60 68 76 84 92 100 108 116 124 132 140   -- 16 slots, 8 apart
```

**Eight slots a scanline = sixteen characters; the thirty-two of the thread's title are TWO
scanlines interleaved**, a venetian blind, and 128 px / 32 characters is exactly the 4 px the
nibbles say. Nine writes did not mean nine drawn slots, and reading the count off the listing gave
eighteen and thirty-six here until the pixels were counted.

**What the blind does NOT cost is a blank line.** All eleven scanlines of each text row draw; the
alternation is between odd and even COLUMNS, not between drawing and repositioning, because the
re-strobes rebuild the positions inside the drawing line itself. What it does cost is density: each
character appears on every other scanline, which is why the glyphs read as dotted.

**The arithmetic that decides whether a design fits:** slots come from re-strobing, but bytes come
from the line's cycles. At six cycles a write a line affords about ten writes, and how many letters
that is depends entirely on how many fit in a byte — two 4 px letters to a byte is twenty, one 8 px
letter to a byte is ten. Widening the letter costs count at exactly that rate, and no amount of
re-strobing changes it.

## Traps

- **Do not read the glyph bytes from a table indexed by Y.** `lda abs,y` is four cycles against
  three for `lda zp`, and at ten writes a line that is the difference between 72 and 82 of 76. Dense
  text kernels compose their bytes into RAM during VBLANK and the kernel only streams them — which
  is why `cmd/dissect` finds no ROM match for any graphics stream in `36char.bin`.
- **Do not strobe RESxx at cycle 0 or cycle 3 after HMOVE.** The strobe races HMOVE's extra clock
  pulses and the object lands one pixel differently on different consoles; cycles 1 and 2 are safe
  (`reference/atariage/311795`, alex_79 and jetsetilly — the race is modelled in Gopher2600).
- **A strobe in horizontal blank behaves differently from a mid-line one**, and the fixture shows
  both: its re-park strobe (write cycle 21, beam still at −5) leaves the OLD base's copies on the
  line it runs on, so a kernel cannot park and use the new position on the same scanline.
- **Three probes in the originating work concluded a strobe never draws on its own line**, and all
  three were built the same wrong way: the claim is about a copy SEQUENCE restarting, and each of
  them measured a player with ONE copy, where "the first copy" and "the only copy" are the same
  thing and rule 8 eats it. **Measure the mechanism's own precondition.**
